edits.text: 1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant objects to each request to the extent it seeks information protected from disclosure by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, or any other applicable protection. Defendant further objects to any request to the extent it is vague, ambiguous, overbroad, unduly burdensome, or seeks information that is not relevant to any party’s claims or defenses and is not proportional to the needs of the case. These objections are stated only to the extent applicable to a particular request and do not excuse Defendant from responding to any portion of a request that is not subject to an objection.
edits.name: General objections

edits.text: 2. PRODUCTION. Subject to and without waiving the foregoing objections, Defendant will produce non-privileged documents responsive to the requests, if any, in its possession, custody, or control. Any production will be made in accordance with the applicable rules and any agreed or ordered production protocol. Defendant will identify any request for which it is withholding responsive documents on the basis of an objection.
edits.name: Production

edits.text: 3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent required by the applicable rules or any agreement or order, Defendant will identify documents withheld on the basis of privilege or other protection in a privilege log, unless the parties agree otherwise.
edits.name: Privilege log

edits.text: 4. RESERVATION. Defendant reserves the right to supplement or amend these responses as permitted by the applicable rules.
edits.name: Reservation

edits.text: 3. REQUEST-BY-REQUEST RESPONSES AND PRODUCTION. Defendant will provide a separate response to each request, stating whether responsive documents have been located after a reasonable search; whether responsive documents will be produced, and the anticipated production date or dates; and, if responsive documents are being withheld, the specific objection or protection asserted and the scope of the withholding. Any production will be made in accordance with the applicable rules and any agreed or ordered production protocol. These amended responses must be completed with verified, request-specific information before service; this general statement does not represent that responsive documents have or have not been located.

4. PRIVILEGE LOG. For responsive material withheld on the basis of attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or another applicable protection, Defendant will provide a privilege log identifying the withheld material and the basis for withholding to the extent required by the applicable rules, agreement, or order. Any categorical logging or other alternative will be used only if permitted by the applicable rules or agreed to by the parties. The log will be served with the amended responses or on an expressly stated schedule.

5. SEARCH AND SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will conduct a reasonable search for responsive materials within its possession, custody, or control, including materials held by persons or entities from whom Defendant has the legal right to obtain them. Defendant will state the search scope and any material limitations in its amended responses. Defendant reserves the right to supplement or amend these responses as permitted by the applicable rules.

6. REQUEST-BY-REQUEST RESPONSE SCHEDULE. Before service, complete a separate entry for each request in the form: “Request No. __: [Objections, if any, stated with specificity]. Responsive documents located: [yes/no/not yet determined after search]. Production: [documents or categories to be produced and production date, or state none]. Withholding: [whether any responsive material is withheld; specific basis and scope].” Do not serve this schedule with unresolved brackets or unverified statements.
